About Optical Express

Optical Express is a major UK optical and laser eye surgery provider, offering both traditional optician services and specialist refractive surgery. With clinics across the UK and Ireland, they are one of the country's largest providers of laser eye surgery and lens replacement procedures, while also offering standard high-street optical services including eye tests, glasses, and contact lenses.

Optical Express was founded in 1991 in Glasgow, Scotland, initially as a traditional high-street opticians chain. The company grew quickly during the 1990s, opening stores across Scotland and then expanding into England, Wales, and Northern Ireland. What distinguished Optical Express from many competitors was its early recognition of the commercial potential of laser eye surgery, which was emerging as a viable alternative to glasses and contact lenses during the same period. By the mid-1990s, Optical Express had begun investing in laser and refractive surgery services, positioning itself as both a conventional optician and a specialist surgical provider.

The laser eye surgery division of the business grew rapidly through the 2000s, and Optical Express became one of the UK's largest providers of LASIK, LASEK, and other refractive procedures. The company invested heavily in the latest laser technology and recruited experienced ophthalmic surgeons, building a network of dedicated surgical clinics alongside its standard opticians stores. This dual model — combining everyday optical services with specialist surgery — was unusual in the UK market and gave Optical Express a distinctive niche. The company also expanded into lens replacement surgery, offering implantable contact lenses and refractive lens exchange for patients who were not suitable candidates for laser treatment.

Today, Optical Express operates approximately 100 clinics and stores across the United Kingdom and Ireland. The business is privately owned by its founder, David Moulsdale, and employs around 2,000 people. While the laser eye surgery division generates significant revenue and attention, Optical Express continues to operate standard optician services — including NHS eye tests, glasses dispensing, and contact lens fitting — at many of its locations. The company's clinics are typically located in city centres and major towns, and it has invested in advanced diagnostic equipment including OCT scanning, corneal topography, and wavefront aberrometry across its network.

Frequently Asked Questions About Optical Express

Common questions about eye tests, services, and booking at Optical Express.

Is Optical Express only for laser eye surgery?

No, Optical Express offers a full range of standard optician services alongside its laser eye surgery business. You can get NHS and private eye tests, buy glasses and sunglasses, and have contact lenses fitted at many of their locations. However, their reputation and marketing are heavily focused on refractive surgery, so many people are unaware that they also function as a conventional high-street optician.

How much does laser eye surgery cost at Optical Express?

Laser eye surgery prices at Optical Express vary depending on the type of procedure and the complexity of your prescription. Prices typically start from around £595 per eye for standard LASEK and from £1,195 per eye for bladeless LASIK. More advanced procedures using wavefront-guided technology cost more. Optical Express offers free initial consultations and interest-free finance options to help spread the cost.

Is laser eye surgery safe?

Laser eye surgery is one of the most commonly performed elective procedures in the world and has a high safety record. The vast majority of patients achieve excellent results, with many reaching 20/20 vision or better. However, like any surgical procedure, there are risks, including dry eyes, halos around lights, and, rarely, undercorrection or overcorrection. Optical Express will carry out a thorough assessment to determine whether you are a suitable candidate and will explain all potential risks before you decide to proceed.

Can I get a free eye test at Optical Express?

Yes, Optical Express provides free NHS-funded eye tests for all eligible patients. In Scotland, all residents qualify for free NHS eye tests regardless of age or income. In England, Wales, and Northern Ireland, eligibility includes children under 16, adults over 60, those on qualifying benefits, and people with specific medical conditions. Laser eye surgery consultations are also free and carry no obligation.

Where are Optical Express clinics located?

Optical Express operates approximately 100 clinics across the United Kingdom and Ireland, located in major cities and towns including London, Birmingham, Manchester, Leeds, Edinburgh, Glasgow, Aberdeen, Cardiff, Belfast, and many more. Their clinics are typically in city centre locations for easy access.

Can I book an Optical Express appointment through eyetest.co.uk?

Optical Express is not currently available for direct booking through eyetest.co.uk. We list Optical Express on our platform so that customers can compare their services and prices with other opticians. To book an eye test or laser surgery consultation, visit opticalexpress.co.uk or call their booking line directly. We hope to offer Optical Express booking through our platform in the future.

Does Optical Express offer finance for laser eye surgery?

Yes, Optical Express offers a range of finance options for laser eye surgery, including interest-free credit for qualifying patients. Monthly payment plans allow you to spread the cost of treatment over 12 to 60 months. Finance is subject to credit approval, and full details are discussed during the initial consultation.

What is the difference between LASIK and LASEK at Optical Express?

LASIK and LASEK are both types of laser eye surgery, but they differ in how the laser accesses the cornea. LASIK involves creating a thin flap in the corneal surface before reshaping the underlying tissue with a laser — recovery is typically faster, with most patients seeing well within 24 hours. LASEK does not involve a flap; instead, the surface layer of the cornea is gently moved aside, and the laser reshapes the surface directly. LASEK recovery takes a few days longer, but it may be more suitable for patients with thinner corneas. Your Optical Express surgeon will recommend the best option based on your individual assessment.
